title: Spec Document
description: The durable wire contract for a flow-spec artifact — the human-approved interface contract one or more flow-implementation tech pairs build against. This file defines the SHAPE only; the SEMANTICS (when a spec is required, the panel-then-draft procedure, the approval gate, the path+hint briefing discipline) live in the flow-spec skill. software-architect emits this shape as its draft; the orchestrator persists it and calls the deterministic renderer for the human-facing .md. One JSON object per file, at `.crucible/docs/specs/{year}/{month}/{day}/{slug}.json`.

schema_version.description: Contract version. Pinned so a consumer can detect a shape change. The document is durable and may outlive a revision.

id.description: The effort slug — matches the filename (without extension) and the directory it lives under.

status.description: draft: awaiting approval, not yet buildable-against. approved: the human approved it; every flow-implementation pair for this effort builds against it. superseded: a later spec replaced it (this file is kept for history, never edited in place).

created.description: ISO 8601 date only. Frozen at first draft; never changed on approval or later edits.

approved_by.description: Free-text identifying who approved it (the human in this conversation). OMITTED (never null) while status is draft.

approved_at.description: UTC instant (ISO-8601) of approval. OMITTED (never null) while status is draft.

repos_in_scope.description: One entry for a single-repo effort; one per repo for cross-repo work.

goal.description: One paragraph: the outcome this spec exists to produce.

non_goals.description: Explicitly excluded scope, one line per item. The thing that stops silent scope creep.

interface_contracts.description: One entry per repo in repos_in_scope, each becoming that pair's flow-implementation acceptance criterion.

constraints.description: Backward-compat requirements, perf budget, auth model, etc. — one line per item.

decision_log.description: Populated ONLY if a flow-decision panel ran to resolve a genuinely forked interface question. Empty array otherwise — never omitted, so a reader can distinguish 'no fork existed' from 'the field wasn't filled in'.

open_questions.description: Explicitly deferred, non-blocking — things the spec deliberately does not resolve.

repo.description: Repo name or path identifying it within the effort.
Must match a repo value in repos_in_scope.

exposes.description: What this repo offers to other repos/consumers — free-text lines (an endpoint, a schema, a CLI flag); the contract's content is domain-specific, not itself schematized.

consumes.description: What this repo calls into / depends on from another repo in scope.

fork.description: The decision point, framed as a question.

why.description: The reasoning, per the flow-decision panel's resolution.

examples.title: Cross-repo job-submission contract
examples.goal: Let a user submit a long-running job from web-client and track its progress, with core-engine doing the work and service-api brokering between the two.

consumes: core-engine's gRPC SubmitJob/GetJobStatus, per core-engine's own exposes entries
service-api's POST /v1/jobs and GET /v1/jobs/{jobId}, polled every 2s while status is "running"

constraints: jobId is a UUID, generated by core-engine, never client-supplied
status is one of: queued, running, done, failed
open_questions: Whether progress is a percentage or a step count — deferred to core-engine's implementation, not user-visible in v1
